The remark comes amid growing public scrutiny over the extent of government influence in Bollywood , and has reignited discussions about the role of celebrities in political messaging. The controversy traces back to October 2025, when T-Series released the song “Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai,” a tribute to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s achievements, particularly around GST reforms. The video featured prominent actors including Rajkummar Rao, Vikrant Massey , Arshad Warsi , and Varun Dhawan , and quickly became one of the most disliked music videos in Indian history. Social media users criticized the song as political propaganda, and the actors involved faced boycott calls and intense backlash online. On July 21, 2026, Rajkummar Rao posted a message on Instagram in support of students protesting over the NEET paper leak , urging dialogue, peace, and fair education. In the comments section, a user reminded him, “Are bhai, bhul gya kya Modi song mein lead kiya tha tune” (“Bro, did you forget you led the Modi song?”). Rao’s response, though not explicitly detailed in reports, has been widely shared and interpreted as an acknowledgment that he participated in the song under pressure. The exchange has since gone viral, with many seeing it as a rare, candid moment where a Bollywood star hints at the coercive environment actors may face when approached for politically charged projects. The incident has fueled broader conversations about the relationship between the Indian government and the film industry. Critics argue that the “Modi Hai Toh Mumkin Hai” episode exemplifies how state-backed initiatives can leverage celebrity influence to shape public perception, while others defend the actors, suggesting that they may have been compelled to participate for professional or personal reasons. The backlash has also highlighted a growing willingness among the public to question and challenge such collaborations, marking a shift in how audiences engage with celebrity endorsements of political narratives. Rajkummar Rao’s recent support for the student protests, coupled with his Instagram exchange, underscores a complex dynamic: on one hand, he is seen as empathetic to youth concerns; on the other, his past involvement in a controversial political song continues to draw criticism. As debates intensify, the episode serves as a reminder of the delicate balance actors must navigate between personal convictions, professional obligations, and public expectations in an increasingly polarized environment.
